angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 493,947 km at 39.09 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 25.5817 +/- 0.0127 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 39.09 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.71 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Barros et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 23472 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...665A.154B/abstract): 493,947 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.67 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Barros et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 23472 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...665A.154B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4684 +/- 99 K from Barros et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 23472 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...665A.154B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barros et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 23472 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...665A.154B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-23472.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.562, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
